title: Almost no Elizabeth line services running on the last weekend of the month
content: The Elizabeth line will be largely closed over the final weekend of November as Transport for London (TfL) warns passengers to seek alternative routes. The closure affects most of the line on Saturday 28th and Sunday 29th November. In fact, the only bit running will be a two trains an hour shuttle between Reading and Maidenhead, which some folk may remember wasn’t even going to be part of the Elizabeth line when it was first planned. The extension from Maidenhead to Reading was added later. Services in the east and central sections are closed to allow for rail and crossing renewals, and maintenance of overhead line equipment. Services in the west are closed because Network Rail is carrying out a major overhaul of Dolphin Junction near Slough, meaning no trains on any service can enter or leave Paddington. That also means no GWR or Heathrow Express services either. TfL rail replacement bus services will operate on affected sections of the Elizabeth line including: Stratford to Romford Shenfield to Chadwell Heath/Newbury Park Ealing Broadway to Slough Slough to Maidenhead For people heading to Heathrow Airport, the Heathrow Express from Paddington will not run, but the Piccadilly line to Heathrow will be running normally. Trish Ashton, TfL’s Director of Rail, said: “We understand that these closures can impact customers’ journeys and would like to thank them for their patience while this essential work takes place. The work we’re carrying out is essential to maintaining the safety and reliability of the Elizabeth line for the millions of customers who rely it on every year. “We encourage customers to plan ahead, allow extra time for their journeys and check before they travel on TfL’s Journey Planner or the TfL Go app. Rail replacement buses and alternative travel options will be available throughout the closure.” For rail nerds, the closure is also seeing some GWR trains from the west of England and Wales diverted to Euston station.
